title: Gingerbread Waffles
changes_from_base: Half white wholemeal flour, 4 whole eggs, milk with soured cream and molasses, spiced with ginger, nutmeg and cloves; whole eggs instead of whisked whites, and no sugar or vanilla.
summary: Spiced gingerbread waffles rich with molasses and soured cream, best served warm with butter and maple syrup.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
unsalted butter, melted and slightly cooled

steps.title: Heat
steps.text: Heat the waffle iron while you make the batter.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Whisk 120 g plain flour, 113 g white wholemeal flour, 2 tsp baking powder, ½ tsp bicarbonate of soda, ½ tsp salt, 2 tsp ginger, ¼ tsp nutmeg and ¼ tsp cloves together.

steps.title: Whisk
steps.text: In another bowl whisk 4 eggs, 85 g melted butter, 225 ml milk, 113 g soured cream and 64 g molasses.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Mix the wet and dry ingredients together until just combined; a slightly lumpy batter is fine.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Pour about 160-180 ml batter into the greased, hot iron and cook as its instructions say.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve warm with butter and maple syrup.

tips: Don't overmix the batter once the wet and dry ingredients are combined; a few lumps won't affect the finished waffle.
The soured cream and molasses make this batter quite dark, so judge doneness by the iron's timing rather than colour alone.
Reheat leftovers gently so the spiced flavour comes through as warm as when first made.
storage: Keep leftovers airtight in the fridge for several days and reheat before serving. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
